sentences.text: The Intracoastal Waterway runs the length of Florida’s Atlantic coast and along much of the Gulf coast, so you’ll use it constantly.
Its marks carry a small yellow symbol, and that symbol is what you steer by.
A yellow triangle means: treat this mark as red.
A yellow square means: treat it as green.
No matter what color the mark itself is.
Why would the mark’s own color ever disagree?
Because the waterway sometimes shares a channel with an inlet.
The same buoy is green for a boat coming in from the sea, but it may be on the red side for a boat following the waterway.
So on the Intracoastal, look for the yellow.
And returning, on the waterway, means going clockwise around the country: south down the Atlantic side, then north and west along the Gulf.
